# Which papers appear under which theme on the Research page.
# The monthly check uses this file to fill the "Papers on this topic" lists.
#
# Each [section] is one theme. Its options:
#   name:            the theme's name, used in the pull request summary
#   keywords:        looked for in a paper's title and abstract
#   title keywords:  looked for in the title only (for words too common in abstracts)
#   always:          papers that always belong here, one per line
#   never:           papers that never belong here, one per line
#
# Keywords match the start of a word and ignore capitals and hyphens, so
# "stabiliz" finds "stabilization" and "slow-fast" also finds "slow–fast".
# In "always" and "never", identify a paper by its DOI or part of its title.
#
# A paper can appear under several themes, or under none: that is fine for
# one-time collaborations and side projects. A paper that matches no keywords is
# placed under a theme only if it is clearly similar to papers already there; the
# pull request marks those as a best guess, and you can correct them here.
# Papers listed under [no theme] at the bottom never appear on the Research page.

[slow-fast]
name: Slow-fast dynamics and critical transitions
keywords:
    slow-fast, fast-slow, singular perturbation, canard, critical transition,
    time scale, timescale, multiscale, tipping, relaxation oscillation
always:
    10.1016/j.nonrwa.2020.103220

[singularity]
name: Bifurcation, singularity theory, and desingularization
keywords:
    blow-up, blowup, desingulari, singularity, singularities, non-hyperbolic,
    nonhyperbolic, nilpotent, normal form, cusp, umbilic
title keywords:
    bifurcation

[networks]
name: Networked dynamical systems
keywords:
    network, hypergraph, graph, higher-order, consensus, chimera, synchroniz, kuramoto

[control]
name: Control of multiscale and networked systems
keywords:
    controller, control law, feedback control, optimal control, control strategy
title keywords:
    control, stabiliz, port-hamiltonian, region of attraction, model reduction,
    model order reduction

[no theme]
papers:
    10.1016/j.aml.2017.01.005
